And with Ramírez re-upping on a seven-year extension this past winter, he's pretty well locked in as the face of this franchise through at least the end of the decade. He's arguably already one of the players on Cleveland's Mount Rushmore, and he's probably going to go down as the greatest player in this franchise's history when all is said and done.
Detroit Tigers : SS Kevin McGonigle (signed through 2034)

When the Tigers signed McGonigle to an eight-year, $150M extension a whole three weeks into his MLB career, it was a calculated risk. Already, though, it's looking like it could be a preposterously team-friendly contract. He's going to win AL Rookie of the Year and may well finish in the top five of AL MVP voting. He and Max Clark are going to be quite the infield/outfield tandem for years to come.
Kansas City Royals : SS Bobby Witt Jr. (signed through at least 2030)

Since his arrival in 2022, Witt has amassed 120 home runs, 181 stolen bases, an .841 OPS, a pair of Gold Gloves and a batting crown. Save for three-time MVP Aaron Judge and four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani, he has been the most valuable player of the past half-decade. Even if he opts out of the remainder of his contract after 2030, it's likely he would do so as the second-greatest Royal ever, behind only George Brett.
Minnesota Twins : OF Walker Jenkins (has not yet made MLB debut)

Joe Ryan has one year left before he hits free agency. Both Byron Buxton and Royce Lewis will also be hitting the open market after 2028. So unless you're all-in on Brooks Lee or Luke Keaschall becoming stars, it's tough to identify an active Twin who is destined for greatness. They do have a highly touted prospect in Walker Jenkins, though, who has been raking at Triple-A thus far in August. He could be a crucial September call-up and a key piece of this core as early as next season.
Athletics : 1B Nick Kurtz (under team control through 2031)

Kurtz is not one of the four hitters that the A's have managed to sign to an early contract extension, but he also isn't going to reach free agency any time soon. Through his first 204 games in the majors, he clubbed 56 home runs with 152 RBI. And if he can even remotely replicate that for the foreseeable future, the only question is who becomes the other half of Bash Brothers 2.0?
Houston Astros : OF Cam Smith (under team control through 2030)

Of the 17 Astros who have recorded either 230 plate appearances or 55 innings pitched this season, only four are controllable through 2029. Of that quartet, only Cam Smith can reasonably be considered a long-term building block—and even that is questionable. On top of that, the Astros have arguably the least promising farm system among the 30 teams. The outlook could change, but Houston could also be in a bleak position three years from now.
Los Angeles Angels : OF Mike Trout (signed through 2030)

Trout will turn 38 during the 2029 campaign, but can you come up with a better candidate here? Even if they keep both Zach Neto and Nolan Schanuel for as long as they can, both of those former first-round picks will be hitting free agency after 2029 (if they don't sign extensions first). And Trout has been more valuable than both of them this season anyway. He's also currently at 424 home runs and reasonably could get to 500 in 2029.
Seattle Mariners : CF Julio Rodríguez (signed through at least 2029)

After the 2028 season, the Mariners have to decide if they're going to exercise an eight-year club option of at least $240M for 2030-37. If they decline it, he can exercise a five-year, $90M player option for 2030-34. But 2029 would be really awkward if the M's go that route. If they pick up the option, though—which, if they had to decide today, they probably would—they're locking him in as their main man for well into the 2030s.
Texas Rangers : SS Corey Seager (signed through 2031)

Seager will turn 35 early in the 2029 campaign, which is a tough ask for a shortstop who has already endured more than his fair share of injuries over the past nine years. But if not Seager, then whom? An even older Brandon Nimmo? Evan Carter or Wyatt Langford in what presently would be his final year before free agency? Maybe their 20-year-old top prospect will be ready to shine by then, but we'll go with the $325M Seager for now.
Atlanta Braves : CF Michael Harris II (signed through at least 2030)

In addition to our official "Don't Sleep On" pick of Drake Baldwin, don't sleep on Matt Olson becoming an inescapable narrative in 2029. If he continues to play in every game—and if there actually are 162 games played in 2027—he's on track to reach third place behind only Cal Ripken Jr. and Lou Gehrig on MLB's consecutive games played list in early May 2029. But Harris' eight-year, $72M contract (with club options for 2031 and 2032) is the gift that keeps on giving to Atlanta.
Miami Marlins : OF Owen Caissie (under team control through 2031)

The year 2029 could be a make-or-break one for the Marlins, with Otto Lopez, Xavier Edwards, Kyle Stowers, Max Meyer and Eury Pérez all slated to hit free agency that winter. But considering they gave up three years of team control of Edward Cabrera to get Owen Caissie (and two other prospects) this past offseason, they've got to be hoping he'll become a major piece of the puzzle.
New York Mets : OF Juan Soto (signed through at least 2029)

Soto could opt out of the 10 years and $460M left on his contract after 2029, but the Mets could also void the opt out by turning it into a 10-year, $500M deal from that point forward. So, he's probably a Met for life at this point, and they didn't give him $765M in December 2024 for him to not be the face of this franchise in 2029.
Philadelphia Phillies : LHP Cristopher Sánchez (signed through 2031)

The Phillies have six players signed through at least 2030, but four of them—Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber, Trea Turner and Aaron Nola—will be in their age-36 season in 2029. Maybe Harper or Schwarber will still be the star of the show at this point, but let's finally get a pitcher onto the list, yeah? And outside of maybe Tarik Skubal, Cristopher Sánchez has been the best pitcher in baseball since the beginning of last season. His six-year, $104M contract sure is looking like a steal these days.
Washington Nationals : OF James Wood (under team control through 2030)

Had he not landed on the IL with an oblique strain in early August, there was a real chance Wood was going to get to 45 home runs, 100 RBI and 25 stolen bases. That's a line that has been achieved just six times in MLB history, and only by Shohei Othani (twice) in the past 25 years. Not too shabby for a 23-year-old who has also drawn 90 walks this season.
Chicago Cubs : CF Pete Crow-Armstrong (signed through 2032)

Pete Crow-Armstrong vs. Shohei Ohtani for NL MVP has become quite the heated debate, but there's no debating who the face of the Cubs is. They locked in PCA on a six-year, $115M extension just a few days before this season began, meaning he'll cost them, on average, less than $20M per year through 2032. What a steal for a guy who might mess around and join the 40/40 club while winning a Platinum Glove.
Cincinnati Reds : 1B/3B Sal Stewart (under team control through 2031)

2029 is going to be Cincinnati's last year of control on Elly De La Cruz. And given Scott Boras' history of not letting his guys sign extensions before hitting free agency, that isn't likely to change. So there's a good chance Stewart will be the guy for the Reds by three years from now—if he isn't already. With 27 home runs and an MLB-best 96 RBI, he's in a two-horse race with JJ Wetherholt for NL Rookie of the Year.
Milwaukee Brewers : RHP Jacob Misiorowski (under team control through 2031)

Jackson Chourio, Cooper Pratt and No. 1 overall prospect Jesús Made could all be the correct answer here, as position players naturally have a leg up on pitchers in face of the franchise conversations. But Misiorowski isn't just another pitcher. He is a weekly spectacle, 80 percent of the way through arguably the most dominant pitching season in at least a quarter century. If he can stay healthy, he's going to have multiple Cy Youngs by 2029 and will be " the Brewer" much like Clayton Kershaw was " the Dodger" for a while.
Pittsburgh Pirates : SS Konnor Griffin (signed through 2034)

Like De La Cruz in Cincinnati, Paul Skenes is the current face of the franchise in Pittsburgh. However, it feels like a sure thing that 2029 will also be his final season with the Pirates—if they even keep him that long. But Griffin entered 2026 as arguably the top prospect in all of baseball, and his legacy in the Steel City is just getting started. It's a shame that injuries have limited him to just eight games played since the end of May, but he is already a star in the making.
St. Louis Cardinals : IF JJ Wetherholt (signed through 2034)

Joshua Báez made a historic one-game first impression with three home runs in his MLB debut last week, but Wetherholt has made the best full-season first impression in St. Louis since Albert Pujols won Rookie of the Year in 2001. He is the biggest reason the Cardinals have a tangible postseason pulse right now, and they've already locked him in for the next eight years for barely $14M a pop.
Arizona Diamondbacks : OF Corbin Carroll (signed through at least 2030)

Carroll just turned 26 on Friday, yet he is already MLB's active leader in career triples with 58. There's a chance he'll end up with 20 triples, 20 home runs and 20 stolen bases this season, which hasn't been done since 2007. And he's still just getting started. Wherever the Snakes go from here, he is the foundation.
Colorado Rockies : 1B T.J. Rumfield (under team control through 2031)

The only player for the Rockies with a known salary in 2029 is Ezequiel Tovar, and he simply has not been the same player since they inked him to a seven-year, $63.5M extension in 2024. But maybe Rumfield becomes the building block this franchise has been looking for since running off Nolan Arenado and Trevor Story. They got Rumfield from the Yankees in January for the low price of Angel Chivilli, and he has quickly become their co-MVP alongside Hunter Goodman, whose last year of arbitration eligibility will be in 2029.
Los Angeles Dodgers : DH/RHP Shohei Ohtani (signed through 2033)

Whether he'll still be pitching in 2029 remains to be seen, but the four-time MVP is the face of Major League Baseball right now. It's hard to imagine he will not still be the face of the Dodgers in 2029, when he will be in his age-34 season with four years remaining on his $700M contract. Heck, 2029 could even be when he passes Barry Bonds for most MVP trophies in a career. (Though, we shall see if he can edge out PCA for No. 5 this year.)
San Diego Padres : RF Fernando Tatis Jr. (signed through 2034)

Two months into this season, Tatis' 14-year contract was starting to look like more of a curse than a gift. But after posting a .595 OPS through his first 50 games, he has been north of .900 over the past 76 contests, mashing his own home runs when not busy robbing others' grand slams. He might already be the greatest Padre not named Tony Gwynn or Trevor Hoffman, and it probably won't be long before he leaves Hoffman in the dust.
San Francisco Giants : 1B/DH Bryce Eldridge (under team control through 2031)

The Giants will still be paying Rafael Devers, Matt Chapman and Willy Adames a ton of money through 2029 and beyond, but it rather feels like "Bryce Eldridge or bust" as far as a face of the franchise is concerned. Maybe Devers flips that script and wins back over the fans, but this rookie already looks the part in his age-21 campaign.

articles.title: Little League World Series 2026 Friday Scores, Bracket Results and Highlights
articles.summary: The 2026 Little League World Series continued Friday with a loaded slate after rain delays pushed back a handful of games.
articles.body:
The 2026 Little League World Series continued Friday with a loaded slate after rain delays pushed back a handful of games.

That meant there were eight games on schedule with four international matches and four between American teams.

Here is a look at the full schedule and results. The bracket can be found in full on the Little League World Series website .

Little League World Series 2026 Monday Schedule, TV Info and Bracket Predictions

Mountain (Nevada) def. Great Lakes (Ohio), 6-5

Midwest (Iowa) def. West (California), 1-0

Northwest (Washington) def. Southwest (Texas), 4-3

Metro (New Jersey) def. Mid-Atlantic (Pennsylvania), 3-1

Mexico wasted no time pushing three runs across the board in the first inning and never looked back on the way to a commanding 7-1 victory over Australia.

Jorge Fonseca led the way with three runs scored, while Gareth Garcia notched two RBI. Mexico also used plenty of small ball to generate the runs and capitalized on its opportunities.

Fonseca did more than just score offensively.

He also struck out six and allowed just two hits in three shutout innings on the mound. From there, Esteban Bautista and Paul Lavenant combined to allow just one run in the final three innings.

The day's first real dramatics came in Nevada's 6-5 victory over Ohio.

Both teams battled back and forth throughout the game, but Nevada had the last chance at the plate. And it took full advantage when Hudson Cowley delivered a walk-off single to play the role of hero.

Ohio built a 2-0 lead and then a 5-2 advantage, but Nevada continued to battle back. The victors scored two runs in the bottom of the fourth, another in the bottom of the fifth and the winner in the sixth.

Maddox Bryan also played well with two hits and two RBI before Cowley ended things with his hit.

Iowa didn't just defeat California 1-0 in Friday's matchup.

Cooper Thissen did much of the heavy lifting in the combined no-hitter with 15 strikeouts in 5.1 innings of work. However, Anthony Johnson Jr. had to finish the job and did so in clutch fashion with a bases-loaded strikeout to end the game and preserve the 1-0 advantage.

Pitching like that would have been enough to make Thissen the hero, but he also delivered a solo homer in the first inning for the game's only run.

It was a Shohei Ohtani-like performance from the two-way star, and Iowa came away with the win as a result.

The combined no-hitters weren't limited to the United States side of the bracket.

Curaçao defeated Japan 6-0 and didn't allow a single hit in the process. Jaymiell Martina started things by striking out seven in 4.2 innings of work, while Giendry Ryan struck out four in the final 1.1 innings to put the finishing touches on the masterpiece.

Curaçao didn't need much offense with the pitching brilliance leading the way, but it got plenty on the way to six runs.

Steven Felix notched two RBI, while Raymiel Antonia went 2-for-2 with a run scored.

It would have been difficult to script a more dramatic finish to Washington's 4-3 victory over Texas than what unfolded Friday.

It seemed as if Texas was going to win with some late-game heroics when it loaded the bases with nobody out in the bottom half of the sixth inning, but pitcher Kasen Workman escaped the jam by inducing two groundouts and a fly out to secure the win.

Paxton Hansen also pitched a shutout inning in relief for Washington, which helped it preserve its early advantage.

Workman made an impact offensively with two RBI as well, while Winston Weaver and Evan Yarbrough each notched an RBI as well.

Nicaragua's 6-4 victory over Panama marked yet another game that came down to the final batter in Friday's slate.

First, Nicaragua scored four runs in the top half of the sixth inning to take the 6-3 lead. However, Panama pushed a run across in the bottom half of the frame and had the bases loaded before Nicaragua won it with a play at the plate on a wild pitch.

Kendry Arauz Roque drove in two runs with the bat and pitched the first 3.2 innings for the victors, while Moises Estrada Juarez allowed just one run in two innings.

Lucas Olmos and Jadhier Rivera each had two hits for Panama, but it wasn't enough to overcome the final deficit.

New Jersey took an early lead and never relinquished it during a 3-1 victory over Pennsylvania.

In the bottom of the second inning, New Jersey gained a 2-0 advantage after Jett Bridges scored on a wild pitch and Joey Dwyer drove in AJ Tapia with a single.

New Jersey struck again in the bottom of the fourth, as Mason Rincon hit a solo home run to right field.

Pennsylvania finally responded once Dillon DiGiulio scored on an error in the fifth inning. The team also had runners at second and third in the same frame, but couldn't drive them in.

New Jersey ultimately held on for the win, as Chase Klimkowski pitched 5.1 innings without allowing an earned run. Klimkowski also recorded six strikeouts.

Led by a dominant pitching performance, Korea took down Czechia in the final matchup of the day.

Both teams were tied 0-0 through two innings of action, although Korea took a 1-0 lead in the top of the third.

After Ki Hyun Jung opened the inning with a single and advanced to second on an error, he stole third and scored on a wild pitch to give his team an early advantage.

Another error allowed Ju Won Kim to score in the top of the fifth inning before Korea added three insurance runs in the sixth, highlighted by a two-run homer from Hyun Been Han.

Do Yoon Kim, Ha Jun Ju and Ji Hwan Hong combined to allow just one hit in six scoreless innings of work while racking up 11 total strikeouts.

articles.title: New Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Injury Update Reveals Blue Jays Star's Return Timeline After Concussion
articles.summary: Toronto Blue Jays star Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is on track to return Saturday from the concussion that has sidelined him since Aug. 14.
articles.body:
Toronto Blue Jays star Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is on track to return Saturday from the concussion that has sidelined him since Aug. 14.

Guerrero passed his final concussion tests and is "feeling good today," Blue Jays manager John Schneider told reporters Friday (h/t MLB.com's Keegan Matheson and broadcaster Hazel Mae ).

Schneider said Guerrero is expected to hit in cages Friday before returning to the lineup the following day, per Mae.

The second game of the Blue Jays' weekend series against the New York Yankees is scheduled for 1:35 p.m. ET Saturday in the Bronx.

Guerrero underwent concussion testing after his head took contact from the knee of Yankees shortstop George Lombard Jr. in a collision at third base on Aug. 14.

He was placed on the seven-day concussion injured list the following day, making Saturday the first day he will be eligible for return.

Guerrero took the first step toward a return by serving as DH for Single-A Dunedin Thursday night.

He went 1-for-1 with an RBI double and drew two walks before he was removed from the game in the fourth inning.

Guerrero has batted .263 with seven home runs through 115 games to mark his least productive campaign since 2020.

The Blue Jays have gone 3-2 since Guerrero's concussion as Alejandro Kirk took over Guerrero's usual spot in the three hole while rookie Charles McAdoo has been productive throughout the lineup.

"We're going to continue to be a team that's built around him, and however he fits in, he's going to understand," Schneider said about where Guerrero would slot back into the lineup in a Friday appearance on Sportsnet 590 The Fan . "It's not gonna hurt his feelings if he's hitting second or if he's hitting third. He gets it. He's watching how we're playing."

Whether the Blue Jays are able to build on their momentum while slotting Guerrero back into the lineup could be key to the club's playoff hopes. Toronto is heading into the weekend series against the Yankees half a game back of both the Minnesota Twins and Texas Rangers for the final Wild Card spot in the AL.

articles.title: Dodgers President Addresses Sale Rumors After Mark Walter Sells Lakers for Record $12.5B
articles.summary: In the wake of Mark Walter's surprise decision to sell the Los Angeles Lakers, there doesn't appear to be any indication within the Los Angeles Dodgers organization that they are going to change owners.
articles.body:
In the wake of Mark Walter's surprise decision to sell the Los Angeles Lakers, there doesn't appear to be any indication within the Los Angeles Dodgers organization that they are going to change owners.

Dodgers president Stan Kasten dismissed any rumors of a sale when asked about the situation on Friday.

"The Dodgers are not being sold. They're not for sale. There's no process that has been started to sell it, period," Kasten told reporters . "We are planning only to win."

Kasten went on to explain that Walter views the Dodgers differently than he did the Lakers.

"I can't tell you how important the Dodgers are to Mark," Kasten said. "The Lakers thing? The Lakers were important to him too, but it's kind of an extraordinary opportunity, which he took."

Walter, whose purchase of the Lakers was approved by the NBA board of governors in October 2025, agreed to sell the franchise at a record $12.5 billion valuation to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner on Aug. 12.

Given the lack of any hint the Lakers were even on the market, there was immediate speculation about the possibility of the Dodgers being available.

Kasten previously said the Lakers' sale was "not really a Dodgers story" because they are "completely separate" and there were "no changes" to what the MLB club was doing.

A Dodgers sale could have huge ramifications on MLB beyond who is in charge of the franchise. Shohei Ohtani negotiated into his contract a "key man" clause that allows him to opt out if Walter or president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman were to leave the organization.

Per The Athletic's Sam Blum and Stephen J. Nesbitt , Ohtani would be "unlikely" to use his opt-out if it came into play. He is under contract through the 2033 season, though he will be owed $680 million in deferred money that gets paid out over 10 years starting in 2034.

Walter has been the controlling owner of the Dodgers since 2012. He was part of the Guggenheim Baseball Management group that purchased the club from Frank McCourt for $2.15 billion , a record sale price at the time for an MLB franchise.

The Dodgers have made the playoffs every year during Walter's tenure as controlling owner. They have won three World Series titles in five appearances, including each of the last two years.

If the Dodgers win a World Series again this season, they will become the first team to three-peat since the New York Yankees from 1998-2000.

A Dodgers sale could have huge ramifications on MLB beyond who is in charge of the franchise. Shohei Ohtani negotiated into his contract a "key man" clause that allows him to opt out if Walter or president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman were to leave the organization.

Per The Athletic's Sam Blum and Stephen J. Nesbitt , Ohtani would be "unlikely" to use his opt-out if it came into play. He is under contract through the 2033 season, though he will be owed $680 million in deferred money that gets paid out over 10 years starting in 2034.

Walter has been the controlling owner of the Dodgers since 2012. He was part of the Guggenheim Baseball Management group that purchased the club from Frank McCourt for $2.15 billion , a record sale price at the time for an MLB franchise.
The Dodgers have made the playoffs every year during Walter's tenure as controlling owner. They have won three World Series titles in five appearances, including each of the last two years.
If the Dodgers win a World Series again this season, they will become the first team to three-peat since the New York Yankees from 1998-2000.

articles.title: Andy Pages Injured by HPB, Latest on Dodgers Star After Concern of Season-Ending Fracture in Hand
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers' mood after a 5-4 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates on Friday was tempered by the news that Andy Pages suffered a fracture on the back of his left hand after being hit by a pitch.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' mood after a 5-4 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates on Friday was tempered by the news that Andy Pages suffered a fracture on the back of his left hand after being hit by a pitch.

Dodgers manager Dave Roberts revealed the news of Pages' injury after the game, but the expectation is he won't miss the rest of the season.

"It's not season-ending because obviously things like that it's four or five weeks," Roberts told reporters . "I would expect him back, knowing him, on the earlier side. There's still time in the season for him to be back. I feel for him because he's having such a good year."

Pages was hit on the back of his hand by a pitch clocked at 100 mph from Pirates starter Bubba Chandler in the bottom of the third inning.

Roberts did note there's a possibility Pages could require surgery, but it's not believed that would change his return timeline.

Pages actually stayed in the game through the fourth inning before Enrique Hernández replaced him in center to start the top of the fifth.

A four-week timeline would have Pages back for the final week of the regular season. The Dodgers' nine-game lead in the NL West gives them the ability to avoid feeling like they have to rush him back, but they could look to get him some at-bats in games before the playoffs if he is healthy.

The regular season ends on Sept. 27. If the Dodgers finish as one of the top two seeds in the NL, they wouldn't play until Oct. 3 when the Division Series begins.

Los Angeles currently has a three game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League. The Dodgers are only two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in MLB, but Milwaukee holds the tiebreaker thanks to a 4-3 head-to-head record.

The news about Pages comes as the Dodgers are uncertain about Dalton Rushing's status for the rest of the regular season due to a partially torn UCL.

Rushing did say this week he is progressing to be able to throw with the hope he can catch again at some point in September.

Pages' injury also interrupts what has been a terrific season for him. The 25-year-old is hitting .272/.338/.458 with 21 homers in 128 games. He is also an elite defensive centerfielder with 17 defensive runs saved, second-most at the position behind Ceddanne Rafaela (19).

Hernández and Tommy Edman will likely receive the bulk of the playing time in center until Pages can return.

articles.title: Kade Anderson's Final Box-Score Stats & Highlights From MLB Debut for Mariners vs. Cubs
articles.summary: Kade Anderson showed flashes of why he is MLB's top pitching prospect in his Saturday night debut for the Seattle Mariners.
articles.body:
Kade Anderson showed flashes of why he is MLB's top pitching prospect in his Saturday night debut for the Seattle Mariners.

Anderson, the third pick of the 2025 draft, threw 53 strikes on 81 pitches on his way to striking out five batters before he was pulled from his sixth inning against the Chicago Cubs.

Here's a look at how the 22-year-old left-hander performed while helping the Mariners to a 5-4 win against the visiting Cubs.

Anderson started out his MLB debut with a 1-2-3 first inning highlighted by forcing Cubs star Alex Bregman into a swinging strikeout.

Thanks to five strikeouts and strong defense from Randy Arozarena in the third frame, Anderson made it through four scoreless innings as the Mariners climbed out to a 1-0 lead.

Anderson gave up his first run of the night after walking leadoff batter Tyrone Taylor, who scored later in the frame on a sacrifice fly from Kevin Alcántara.

He ran into trouble after allowing back-to-back home runs from Bregman and Michael Busch in the top of the sixth, at which point he was pulled for Carlos Vargas.

Anderson has spent this season pitching for Double-A Arkansas, where he has averaged under 5.2 innings per game in 18 appearances while marking a 1.06 ERA.

The Mariners will need to decide whether to take out Anderson earlier from his next MLB appearance, which could potentially take place as soon as next weekend against the Toronto Blue Jays.

articles.summary: The intensity and drama of the 2026 Little League World Series (LLWS) has been ratcheted up this weekend. Saturday brought the first elimination games of the tournament, and Sunday will bring the spotlight to contenders from the winners' brackets.

The intensity and drama of the 2026 Little League World Series (LLWS) has been ratcheted up this weekend. Saturday brought the first elimination games of the tournament, and Sunday will bring the spotlight to contenders from the winners' brackets.

The double-elimination is once again broken down into United States and International brackets. The winner of each will face off in the LLWS Championship on Sunday, August 30.

Here, you'll find a preview of Sunday's action—which includes the MLB Little League Classic—along with tournament information, scheduling info, and some predictions.

Australia Region: Ryde Little League (Sydney, New South Wales)

Sunday's opener will pit Paseo Verde Little League of Henderson, Nevada (Mountain Region) against Soundview Little League of Tacoma, Washington.

Soundview has taken the tough road to this point, notching 2-0 and 4-3 victories over the Southeast and Southwest regions, respectively. Paseo Verde, meanwhile, delivered a 6-5 walk-off win over the Great Lakes on Friday to advance. Both teams have shown the ability to win tight contests, so this should be a fun matchup to start the day.

The second morning match will feature Municipal De Tijuana Little League of Tijuana in a matchup with Ministerio Sobre Las Alas Del Águila Little League of León, Nicaragua.

On paper, this is a less-even matchup. The Latin America representative eked through close contests against the Caribbean and Panama, while Mexico is coming off a 7-1 romp over Australia.

Game 3 will feature Davenport Northwest Little League of Davenport, Iowa, a team that is coming off a combined no-hitter against the West region. Davenport will take on a Bayonne Central Little League team that has notched 2-1 and 3-1 victories over the New England and Mid-Atlantic regions.

Bayonne's first victory of the tournament came in walk-off fashion.

Sunday's last tournament game will pit West Seoul Little League of South Korea against Pariba Little League of Willemstad, Curaçao.

Willemstad has produced two of the last four LLWC runners-up, and Pariba is coming off a dominant 6-0 shutout of Japan. However, West Seoul has looked like one of the best squads in the tournament while winning 7-0 and 5-0 against Canada and Europe-Africa, respectively.

Sunday's nightcap will be Major League Baseball's annual Little League Classic, featuring the Atlanta Braves and Milwaukee Brewers at historic Bowman Field.

articles.title: New Shohei Ohtani Pitching Update, Dodgers' Dave Roberts Reveals Timeline for Star to Pitch in Game
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts believes it could only be a matter of days before Shohei Ohtani is back to pitching in MLB games.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts believes it could only be a matter of days before Shohei Ohtani is back to pitching in MLB games.

Roberts told reporters Sunday that Ohtani's return to the mound could arrive as early as next week.

According to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya and Katie Woo , Los Angeles is considering starting Ohtani and having him throw one inning against the Detroit Tigers on Aug. 30.

The four-time MVP had a throwing session against hitters on Saturday at Dodger Stadium.

Ohtani hasn't pitched since the Dodgers' 4-3 win over the San Diego Padres on July 3. He was initially sidelined because of knee trouble, and team doctors also flagged a biceps injury in his throwing arm.

Ohtani has continued to serve as the designated hitter in the interim, and his performance hasn't suffered much despite not being at 100 percent. Across 20 games so far in August, he has six home runs and a .282/.371/.564 slash line.

Welcoming the six-time All-Star back as a two-way player would be a huge boost to the starting rotation.

The Dodgers' acquisition of Tarik Skubal was a case of the rich getting richer, but the pitching staff was also an area of concern. At the time of the trade, the trio of Ohtani, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow were unavailable, while Justin Wrobleski had soared past his career high for innings in a single MLB season.

L.A. has since welcomed Snell back from the injured list, but Wrobleski landed on the IL with left forearm inflammation.

For as much as some fans think a three-peat is almost preordained, the Dodgers pitching staff isn't in a great place right now. The situation is much different if Ohtani gets the green light and remains the player who posted a 1.79 ERA and averaged 10 strikeouts per nine innings before going down.

articles.title: New 2026 MLB Playoff Seeding and World Series Predictions With 5 Weeks to Go
articles.summary: With barely a month remaining until the 2026 MLB postseason begins, the bracket is beginning to feel a bit more solidified.
articles.body:
With barely a month remaining until the 2026 MLB postseason begins, the bracket is beginning to feel a bit more solidified.

Not all 12 spots in the field, mind you. Arizona vs. San Diego for the NL's No. 6 seed looks destined to come right down to the wire, the AL West remains a three-way free-for-all, and you may as well just throw a dart at your best guess for the third and final AL wild-card spot.

However, nine teams have at least a 90 percent chance of making the playoffs, and the rest is slowly but surely taking shape.

What will the final playoff seeding look like?

And which teams are best equipped to win the whole shebang?

We'll go division-by-division (plus a wild card breakdown) through the current state of each league before offering up our latest October predictions.

Consensus Division Odds via Baseball-Reference, FanGraphs and PECOTA (as of Sunday a.m.)

Boston @ Tampa Bay (3 games, Sept. 18-20)

Tampa Bay @ New York (4 games, Sept. 22-24)

Projected Winner: Tampa Bay Rays (earning No. 1 seed)

The Yankees have certainly kept things interesting, gaining 3.5 games on the Rays in a hurry this past week by virtue of a five-game winning streak. But Tampa Bay has managed to counter-punch every Yankees punch for two months at this point, alone in first place on a daily basis going back to June 28.

That series at Yankee Stadium next month looms all sorts of large, though.

The Bronx Bombers are certainly hoping to have Aaron Judge and Max Fried back and at full strength by the time they square off for four games in three days. And should the Yankees sweep that series, they would effectively be gaining 4.5 games on the Rays, as that would also give them a 7-6 edge in the season series for potential tie-breaking purposes.

However, the Rays have done such a phenomenal job of avoiding prolonged cold spells that dropping four straight in New York feels unlikely. And, who knows, they may have already clinched the division by the time that series begins.

Chicago @ Minnesota (3 games, Aug. 28-30)

Detroit @ Minnesota (3 games, Aug. 31-Sept. 2)

Minnesota @ Chicago (3 games, Sept. 4-6)

Detroit @ Cleveland (4 games, Sept. 4-6)

Minnesota @ Detroit (3 games, Sept. 7-9)

Cleveland @ Minnesota (3 games, Sept. 11-13)

Chicago @ Cleveland (3 games, Sept. 14-16)

Detroit @ Chicago (4 games, Sept. 17-20)

Projected Winner: Chicago White Sox (earning No. 2 seed)

As the lone division with four teams plausibly still in the running, the AL Central has, by far, the longest list of remaining head-to-head series that could make a major difference.

In fact, after facing the A's for the next few days, the Twins are about to embark upon a stretch of 15 consecutive games against the White Sox (six), Tigers (six) and Guardians (three). They could go from 5.5 games back to practically running away with this division if they were to catch fire.

At this point, though, it's tough to bet against the White Sox and what has been the highest scoring offense in the American League.

Never would have guessed five months ago that any part of that statement would be true, and we definitely do still have questions about this team's staying power in October with this pitching staff. But they just keep hanging around a few games above .500, which no one else in this division seems capable of doing.

Texas Rangers: 65-66 (Houston holds H2H tiebreaker)

Houston @ Seattle (2 games, Sept. 22-23)

Projected Winner: Seattle Mariners (earning No. 3 seed)

Even before the back-to-back walk-off wins over the Cubs this past weekend, there was one big reason to believe the Mariners might be able to win this thing in spite of their season-long mediocrity: remaining strength of schedule.

The five key games listed above are all home games for the M's. Of the other 26 games left on their slate, 17 come against either the A's (seven), the Angels (seven) or the Rockies (three)—otherwise known as the three worst teams in the majors.

The other three series are against the Phillies, Red Sox and Blue Jays, so we'll see how they fare in those games against teams battling for wild-card spots. Even so, it is the easiest remaining schedule in all of baseball, while both the Rangers and Astros have relatively difficult paths to the finish line.

Can they finally wake up and at least start to resemble the team they were supposed to be? Or are they going to go something like 7-10 against that 17-game gift from the schedule-makers to bring this disappointing season to a depressing end?

Against our better judgment, we're projecting the former.

Current Standings (excluding our projected division winners)

Consensus Postseason Odds via Baseball-Reference, FanGraphs and PECOTA (as of Sunday a.m.)

Projected Wild Card Teams: New York Yankees as No. 4 seed, Boston Red Sox as No. 5 seed and Toronto Blue Jays as No. 6 seed

The Yankees and the Red Sox pretty well have playoff spots locked up.

Most likely, at least one of the teams from this cluster of mediocrity is going to go on a bit of a run through these final five weeks to end up a few games above .500. And if remaining schedule strength is influencing our forecast in the AL West, it should probably be the difference maker here, too.

To that end, while the Mariners technically have the easiest remaining schedule in terms of combined winning percentage of all remaining opponents, one could very easily argue that it's actually the Blue Jays who have the easiest remaining schedule, as all 30 of their remaining games come against teams who are currently below .500.

After 13 consecutive games against the Rays, Red Sox and Yankees over the past two weeks, they no longer have any games left against those division rivals. They also don't face the White Sox, they don't face the Astros and their only interleague matchup left on the docket is a home series against the Reds.

Can't ask for much better than that. We'll see if they take advantage.

Atlanta @ Philadelphia (4 games, Sept. 4-7)

Philadelphia @ Atlanta (3 games, Sept. 11-13)

Projected Winner: Atlanta Braves (earning No. 3 seed)

Not since April 13 has Atlanta led this division by a margin of less than two games.

Yet, what was a 9.5 game lead less than two weeks ago has turned into a possible photo finish, as the Phillies have gone 16-5 thus far in August with seven massive head-to-head games on the horizon.

Can the Braves weather the storm and perhaps even re-assert their legitimacy as a World Series contender by winning both of those series against the Phillies—as they also won the previous two head-to-head series this season?

It will be interesting to see how the starting rotations line up for those showdowns. If both weather and injuries cooperate between now and then, it's looking like Philadelphia will have Cristopher Sánchez and Zack Wheeler on the mound for the first two games at home, while Atlanta is projected to counter with Chris Sale and Martín Pérez.

In the immortal words of Bart Scott: Can't wait!

Consensus Division Odds via Baseball-Reference, FanGraphs and PECOTA (as of Sunday AM)

Milwaukee @ Chicago (4 games, Aug. 31-Sept. 3)

Chicago @ Milwaukee (3 games, Sept. 7-9)

Projected Winner: Milwaukee Brewers (earning No. 2 seed)

For a minute there recently, this race got interesting for the first time in a long time.

After leading the NL Central by at least 3.5 games (though never more than 7.5 games) on a daily basis from May 26 through August 11, the Brewers slipped just a little bit, getting swept by the Padres while the Cubs won three straight to get the margin back down to 3.0 games.

But the Brew Crew bounced back, taking three of four from the Dodgers before winning series against both the Mariners and Braves to push back ahead by what might be an insurmountable margin.

They do have seven head-to-head battles remaining. However, unless Chicago goes at least 5-2 in those games, we're probably done here.

San Diego @ Los Angeles (3 games, Sept. 22-24)

Projected Winner: Los Angeles Dodgers (earning No. 1 seed)

It'd be fun to pretend there's a race worth mentioning here, but there isn't. Not only do the Dodgers have the biggest lead of any current division leader, but they have the easiest remaining schedule among the teams in the NL West.

They also have a much easier schedule than the Brewers, which is why we have them projected to finish ahead of Milwaukee in the race for home-field advantage throughout the postseason.

With Tyler Glasnow set to return this week while Shohei Ohtani is nearing a return to the mound of his own, it almost feels inevitable that the Dodgers—who already have won five games in a row—are about to go on the type of tear that reminds everyone why this team was the overwhelming World Series favorite before the regular season began.

Projected Wild Card Teams: Chicago Cubs as No. 4 seed, Philadelphia Phillies as No. 5 seed and San Diego Padres as No. 6 seed

While the race for the final spot in the American League bracket is an eight-car pile-up of teams who don't feel like a legitimate threat to actually do any damage if they make it to October, the National League is shaping up to be a two-horse race out of the NL West.

And here's the fun news: The only remaining series between the Padres and Diamondbacks takes place in San Diego over the final weekend of the regular season, with the season series currently split 5-5.

The Padres already have a two-game lead, though, and they've been the best team in baseball over the past month, sitting at 21-7 dating back to July 24. The once hapless offense has come to life in a big way in recent weeks, and there's still hope that both Joe Musgrove and Nick Pivetta will make it back onto the mound before it's too late.

Whether either of those pitchers can get stretched out enough to start remains to be seen. But even if they're coming back as middle/long relievers, maybe they help bridge the gap to more Mason Miller saves en route to a spot in the postseason.

No. 3 Seattle Mariners over No. 6 Toronto Blue Jays No. 5 Boston Red Sox over No. 4 New York Yankees

No. 5 Boston Red Sox over No. 1 Tampa Bay Rays No. 3 Seattle Mariners over No. 2 Chicago White Sox

ALCS : No. 5 Boston Red Sox over No. 3 Seattle Mariners

If this is actually the way the seeding plays out, how fun would that Wild Card Round be?

A rematch of last year's ALCS and arguably the fiercest rivalry in the sport that also happens to be a rematch from last year's wild card round?

In particular, Boston vs. New York is the one with potential World Series implications, as those certainly feel like the two best teams in the American League, if healthy.

All due respect to Tampa Bay, but Drew Rasmussen, Nick Martinez and Shane McClanahan don't pack the same punch as Cam Schittler, Gerrit Cole and Max Fried/Carlos Rodón. And no one in the sport has been hotter over the past two months than the Red Sox, at 39-13 in their last 52 games.

Maybe they peaked too early and they're going to flame out before the games truly matter, but betting against Boston coming out of this half of the bracket would feel like a mistake. (And that's without even accounting for the fact that they might get both Roman Anthony and Garrett Crochet back before the regular season ends.)

No. 6 San Diego Padres over No. 3 Atlanta Braves No. 5 Philadelphia Phillies over No. 4 Chicago Cubs

No. 1 Los Angeles Dodgers over No. 5 Philadelphia Phillies No. 2 Milwaukee Brewers over No. 6 San Diego Padres

NLCS : No. 1 Los Angeles Dodgers over No. 2 Milwaukee Brewers

The biggest X-factor on the NL half of the bracket is how much the Phillies will get outside of their big six of Cristopher Sánchez, Zack Wheeler, Jesús Luzardo, Jhoan Duran, Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper.

In winning 16 of their first 21 games of August, they've gotten a ton of production from Bryson Stott, Alec Bohm, Justin Crawford and trade deadline acquisition Luis Arraez, not to mention four straight solid outings from Aaron Nola. If that continues, they could be the perfect foil to the Dodgers and a fantastic candidate to win the World Series.

The Brewers are also a more legitimate threat to the LA dynasty than they were last year, as evidenced by their taking three out of four from the Dodgers a week ago. Granted, they went 6-0 against Los Angeles during the 2025 regular season before getting swept in the NLCS, but their starting rotation has blossomed from "above average" last year to "maybe the best in baseball" this year.

The only thing we're reasonably confident in is that the Cubs don't have the pitching to navigate this gauntlet. But who knows? They could just mash their way through October like the Rangers did in 2023.

Los Angeles Dodgers over Boston Red Sox (in 6 games)

Love them or hate them, the Dodgers are following their tried and true World Series blueprint to a tee:

Assert dominance through the first three months

Sputter for a month or so starting around July 4

Turn things back around in mid-August and enter the postseason on a tear

They're only partway through that third step, but they sure seemed to have snapped out of that 11-17 funk that temporarily dropped them behind Atlanta in the race for the first-round byes.

Blake Snell is back and already reminding everyone of his career splits as a drastically better pitcher in the second half. Tyler Glasnow returns on Tuesday. Tarik Skubal got his first win with the Dodgers on Saturday, a few hours after Shohei Ohtani threw a 30-pitch live batting practice in his quest to resume his unicorn ways. And, of course, Yoshinobu Yamamoto has been their rock all season long.

The thermal exhaust port on this Death Star could be the closer situation if they try to force Edwin Díaz back into that role again when he comes off the IL. Also, the outfield has gotten pretty bleak now that Andy Pages is out indefinitely with a fractured hand.

But the expectation all season long has been that a Dodgers three-peat would be the final straw before a contentious lockout, and that still appears to be the case.

Assert dominance through the first three months
Sputter for a month or so starting around July 4

articles.title: Astros, GM Dana Brown 'Part Ways' Despite Being No. 1 Seed in AL West Standings
articles.summary: The Houston Astros announced Monday they reached a mutual agreement to relieve general manager Dana Brown of his duties.
articles.body:
The Houston Astros announced Monday they reached a mutual agreement to relieve general manager Dana Brown of his duties.

"Over the past four seasons, Dana has helped our organization win two division titles and has led our baseball front office through key scouting, draft and development efforts," owner Jim Crane said. "On behalf of the Astros, I want to thank him for his commitment, energy, and contributions to our organization. We wish he and his family the best."

Meanwhile, Joe Espada's status as manager has not changed, according to Chandler Rome of The Athletic. Per Rome, Espada "has not been told anything about his future beyond this season." He reportedly has not had any conversations about his future.

Brown's exit comes as the Astros are tied for first place in the American League West, though they're a game under .500 (65-66).

Brown's departure has been a long time coming.

Back in June 2024, The Athletic's Chandler Rome wrote how there were questions over how much authority the GM had behind the scenes. Special advisors Reggie Jackson, Jeff Bagwell and Craig Biggio were providing their own input on personnel moves.

Going back two more years, before Brown was hired, Bagwell weighed in to say the organization had leaned too much on analytics despite that approach helping to deliver a pair of World Series titles.

The Hall of Fame first baseman is now part of the group that will share Brown's usual everyday duties.

The Astros' record has steadily gotten worse since their last World Series win in 2022. They registered 90, 88 and 87 wins over the next three years, and now they're on track for their worst finish in a full 162-game season since 2014. Winning the AL West wouldn't hide the fact the roster isn't good enough right now.

Brown undoubtedly has a role in that, but he's not solely to blame for the state of the franchise.

A downturn was inevitable as the key players from their 2017 championship team got older and too expensive to retain over time. The organizational shift in team-building strategy hasn't been a net-positive, either.

Bagwell played a role in the disastrous signing of José Abreu during the 2023 offseason. Crane helped influence the return of Carlos Correa at the 2025 trade deadline, and Correa's sizable contract is aging worse and worse.

In general, the results from Houston's win-now moves speak for themselves. They have a top-10 payroll and one of MLB's worst farm systems . That's a rough combination for a team that looks so far away from seriously contending.

The obvious concern as it relates to the Astros' GM search is whether Crane is willing to let Brown's replacement execute a long-term plan as they see fit.

articles.title: Jacob Young Reacts to 'Spider-Man' Wall Catch After Epic HR Robbery Highlight for Nationals
articles.summary: Washington Nationals center fielder Jacob Young made an incredible catch on Sunday, scaling the wall to deny the Miami Marlins' Heriberto Hernández a home run.
articles.body:
Washington Nationals center fielder Jacob Young made an incredible catch on Sunday, scaling the wall to deny the Miami Marlins' Heriberto Hernández a home run.

Young has been given the Spider-Man nickname in the past, and it sure seemed apt after that grab.

"It's a fun one," he told MLB.com's Perla Paredes regarding the nickname. "But you know, if [I] keep catching the ball, [the fans] can call me whatever they want."

As for scaling the wall to make the grab, Young called it "instinctual" and said that his mindset is to just "go try to catch everything."

"It just kind of ended up in the spot where I like to climb them," he added. "And I'm gonna give myself a chance. And when I looked up, the ball was there, so it was cool to be able to get [Jackson] a couple more innings and keep us in the game."

The Nationals ultimately lost 6-2 anyway, but at least Young provided one of the season's best highlights.

articles.title: Ketel Marte Return Timeline Updated by D-Backs Manager After Stints on Injured, Restricted Lists
articles.summary: The Arizona Diamondbacks have a plan to get second baseman Ketel Marte back on the field after he was placed on the restricted list and then the injured list in the aftermath of him not showing up for a game against the Boston Red Sox.
articles.body:
The Arizona Diamondbacks have a plan to get second baseman Ketel Marte back on the field after he was placed on the restricted list and then the injured list in the aftermath of him not showing up for a game against the Boston Red Sox.

Arizona manager Torey Lovullo said the team hopes to have Marte back in the lineup for its series against the Philadelphia Phillies starting Aug. 31.

"That's what we're thinking about," Lovullo said, per David Brandt of the Associated Press. "I think that will be the 10th day or the 11th day, so there is definitely a strategy to get him back on the field, get him healthy."

Brandt noted the Diamondbacks put Marte on the restricted list after he didn't show up to Fenway Park but eventually moved him to the 10-day injured list because of mild inflammation in his left knee.

The story was once again in the headlines Friday when Marte was seen in a casino during the Diamondbacks' game against the Cincinnati Reds. Lovullo told reporters at the time he was "free to do whatever he wants" as long as he did his rehab work:

According to Brandt, Marte is yet to address his teammates about his disappearance.

"We're trying to create the softest space for him to re-emerge back in this environment," Lovullo said. "That's up to him however he wants to do it. I cannot force a human being to do something that I want to do, or anybody in this room wants to do, or a fan wants to do.

"One of the things that makes Ketel such an extraordinary player is he goes to the beat of his own drum. I respect that."

Marte has appeared in 118 games this season and is slashing .249/.314/.446 with 21 home runs, 67 RBI and four stolen bases.

The 2023 National League Championship Series MVP was also a back-to-back All-Star and Silver Slugger winner in 2024 and 2025. He is a key part of the lineup for an Arizona team hoping to make a late charge.

The Diamondbacks enter Monday's game against the Chicago Cubs two games behind the San Diego Padres for the final wild-card spot in the National League.

articles.title: Cal Raleigh busts out of slump, posts first career 3-homer game to power Mariners past Phillies
articles.summary: Amid a rough 2026 campaign, Raleigh had the biggest night of his career on Monday.
articles.body:
The Seattle Mariners star, after backing up a breakout campaign in 2025 with a very rough go this season, seems to have found his stride again. Raleigh rattled off three home runs to help lift the Mariners to a 9-2 win over the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday night. It was the first three-homer game of his career.

Raleigh opened the night with a two-run shot to right in the first inning at T-Mobile Park, which helped push the Mariners to a 5-1 lead. It was the second home run of the inning for Seattle, too, following Julio Rodríguez 's three-run shot.

Raleigh then followed suit with a deep solo homer in the fifth inning, which extended the Mariners' lead. The first two homers both came off Phillies starter Zack Wheeler .

Cal Raleigh goes deep for the second time in this game 💪 https://t.co/lGEX1Ccf6s pic.twitter.com/YR1srNkvJm — MLB (@MLB) August 25, 2026

Cal Raleigh goes deep for the second time in this game 💪 https://t.co/lGEX1Ccf6s pic.twitter.com/YR1srNkvJm

And finally, Raleigh just barely got his third one over the wall in right field in the seventh inning for good measure. All three of his homers were on nearly identical trajectories.

BIG DUMPER FOR A THIRD TIME 😱 Cal Raleigh has the first 3-homer game of his career! pic.twitter.com/sK00IQgiin — MLB (@MLB) August 25, 2026

BIG DUMPER FOR A THIRD TIME 😱 Cal Raleigh has the first 3-homer game of his career! pic.twitter.com/sK00IQgiin

Raleigh entered Monday night with just a .159 batting average with 47 RBI and only 14 home runs. It was only two weeks ago that Raleigh — who drilled 60 home runs, made his first All-Star team and won the Home Run Derby in 2025 — sounded incredibly down about his play during a losing skid .

"It's not good," he said . "We're not playing well. That starts with me. I'm awful. I've got to find a way to be better and to help bring the guys along. We just gotta play better. We're just playing very, very, very bad baseball in every facet of the game. We gotta pick it up — from the energy standpoint to the execution to the little things in the game that help you win baseball games. We're just not doing those things right now."

Blue Jays add SP Shane Bieber to IL, giving Toronto thin pitching depth in AL wild-card race

Ketel Marte lost the benefit of the doubt long before he showed up to the casino

Mariners shortstop Colt Emerson to have season-ending surgery on left wrist

The win marked Seattle's third in its past four outings, though it entered Monday fresh off a 19-2 beatdown by the Chicago Cubs . The win moved the Mariners to 63-69 on the year, three games back of the AL West-leading Texas Rangers and three games back of the AL's final wild-card spot.

With a little more than a month left in the regular season, they are running out of time to make a move.

One game won't break him out of his funk completely, but Monday's outing was a flash of the greatness that Raleigh showed throughout 2025. Whether that's enough to spark a late rally for the Mariners and get a postseason push going, though, remains to be seen.

articles.title: 15 Yankees Options to Replace Giancarlo Stanton and Find Aaron Judge's Next Co-Star in 2027
articles.summary: It isn't too soon to wonder if we've seen the last of Giancarlo Stanton as a New York Yankee. If we have, the search for his replacement must start now.
articles.body:
It isn't too soon to wonder if we've seen the last of Giancarlo Stanton as a New York Yankee. If we have, the search for his replacement must start now.

Coming into this year, Stanton was a 36-year-old DH with a lengthy injury history. He has since added to it, originally going on the IL with a right calf strain in April and then straining his left calf while trying to run as part of his recovery program. His season, at least, is likely over.

Stanton has missed almost as many games (694) as he's played in (764) since he joined the Yankees in 2018. He has one guaranteed year left on his contract at $25 million, followed by a $10 million buyout on a $25 million club option for 2028.

When B/R ran a poll on what the Yankees should do with Stanton, only 11 percent of respondents were in favor of keeping the 2017 NL MVP. Most preferred him getting released or retiring—the latter would surely require a buyout.

It'll come down to what Stanton wants. If he wants a shot at the 44 home runs he needs to get to 500, he could be granted his release. If he's tired of all the injuries, retirement and the buyout are his best options.

Either way, the Yankees only need to look back to Stanton's 2024 postseason for evidence that even Aaron Judge needs a Robin to his Batman. While they could trust Cody Bellinger , Ben Rice , Luis García Jr. or Spencer Jones to fill that role, they're better off eyeing potential solutions on the free-agent and trade markets.

5 Options for the Yankees in Free Agency

The Pie in the Sky: DH/RHP Shohei Ohtani (LAD)

This is an extreme long shot. Mark Walter has agreed to sell the Los Angeles Lakers, and recent reporting has examined whether that development could affect the Dodgers' ownership outlook.

There is no indication the Dodgers are currently for sale; in fact, The Athletic reported that the signs point against a sale for now. Still, a sale would carry significant implications for Shohei Ohtani, whose 10-year, $700 million contract reportedly includes an opt-out provision if Walter sells the club.

Per Alden Gonzalez of ESPN, the four-time MVP isn't likely to take advantage of that clause. Even if he did, there's no rule that says the Dodgers' subsequent new owners couldn't bring him back.

Still, if there's a one-in-a-million chance of the Yankees having a shot at Ohtani, neither Heaven nor Earth should stand in their way at acquiring the best player baseball has ever known.

The More Likely Targets: LF Randy Arozarena (SEA), 2B Brandon Lowe (PIT), LF Ian Happ (CHC), RF Seiya Suzuki (CHC)

Ohtani aside, these are the best hitters who are slated to hit free agency this winter. It is indeed that weak of a crop.

All of these players are capable of hitting 25 home runs in a season, and Arozarena can add 20 stolen bases. His role in the recent World Baseball Classic controversy could invite added scrutiny in a market like New York. He will also be 32 by Opening Day 2027.

The lefty-hitting, pull-happy Lowe has the best Yankee Stadium profile on paper, but not so much in practice. He has a .650 OPS there for his career, and that's over an ample sample of 44 games.

The switch-hitting Happ is more of a well-rounded type than a slugger, so Suzuki is the better option if all the Yankees want is an impact bat. He's cleared a .800 OPS four years in a row, and has a high of 32 home runs.

10 Options for the Yankees on the Trade Market

The Best Possible Option: DH/LF Yordan Alvarez (HOU)

There was some Alvarez trade buzz earlier this year, and the Houston Astros just decided to part ways with GM Dana Brown. Given this and the dire state of their farm system , maybe we're in for the Astros making a Mookie Betts-style trade.

Even if it's highly unlikely, the Yankees would need to be at the front of the line. Alvarez is another injury-prone guy, yet he's also a guy with a career 168 OPS+ and AL-best marks for AVG, OBP, SLG, OPS, home runs and RBI this year. He also has a 1.133 OPS at Yankee Stadium.

As for the acquisition cost, "huge" doesn't cover it. Alvarez is 29 and owed a modest $53.7 million across 2027 and 2028.

The Funniest Possible Option: DH/1B Rafael Devers (SFG)

Buster Posey was said to be willing to listen on Devers as far back as June . If so, Devers and his $225 million remaining contract are sure to be on the block this winter.

Given how much of a nemesis Devers was to the Yankees (and to Gerrit Cole , specifically) during his time in Boston, one doubts whether the Yankees will be seriously interested. He's also not a can't-miss star at this point. Devers is still just 29, but rocking a .319 OBP and .788 OPS.

However, a powerful lefty will never not be an appealing target for the Yankees. If we end up seeing Devers in pinstripes hitting homers against the Red Sox in support of Cole, we'll have confirmation that we are living in the most chaotic timeline.

Doesn't Hurt to Ask: CF Mike Trout (LAA), CF Byron Buxton (MIN), 1B Bryce Harper (PHI), 1B Munetaka Murakami (CHW)

The Yankees will have an opening in center field once Trent Grisham files for free agency, so it especially makes sense to inquire on Trout and Buxton. Brian Cashman just shouldn't expect to get anywhere on either. Both are institutions with their respective teams, and neither has ever expressed interest in getting traded.

After what Dave Dombrowski said last year , Harper could be a different story. As a two-time MVP who can play first base and right field and who has a powerful left-handed swing, he's a perfect Yankees target on paper. Yet he also has 10-and-5 rights and can block any trade, meaning he would have to approve any move even if the Philadelphia Phillies are willing to talk.

Murakami is a wild card. He's been a hit in his debut with the Chicago White Sox, cranking 29 homers in 95 games. He's only signed through 2027, though, so you wonder if the Pale Hose could entertain offers on the slugger if potential extension talks go nowhere.

Shoot Your Shot: C Hunter Goodman (COL), SS/2B CJ Abrams (WAS), SS Zach Neto (LAA), 2B Ketel Marte (ARI)

Goodman, Abrams and Neto were popular trade candidates before the trade deadline, and the Yankees were connected to at least two of them.

Because George Lombard Jr. has since taken over at shortstop, neither Abrams nor Neto is as good of a fit these days. Either could still hypothetically provide 20-20 upside at second base or third base, though, so it's best not to take them off the board altogether.

Of all the names discussed, Marte is a potential buyer-beware option for the Yankees. He is a three-time All-Star who could fit as an on-field replacement for Jazz Chisholm Jr. However, his recent absence from the Diamondbacks while receiving injury treatment would likely invite added scrutiny in New York.

As such, Goodman remains the best fit for the Yankees. A catcher who can give you 30-homer seasons is a rare thing, and he isn't even a Coors Field product. This year, he has a .900 OPS and 19 of his 34 homers on the road.

Best guess: He won't be on the Yankees next year, but he won't retire either.

As Chris Kirschner of The Athletic noted, Stanton's remaining salary is "within the range that owner Hal Steinbrenner has been willing to absorb to move on from a player." He could therefore be comfortable with simply releasing Stanton, who would then have his pick of 29 other teams with whom to chase 500 homers.

Bold Prediction: Stanton ends up with the San Diego Padres and finishes with 470 career home runs.

Who (If Anyone) Will Replace Stanton in New York?

He's not the most interesting option for the Yankees, but Goodman is the right guy for them.

Unless they want to trust in Austin Wells' recent surge to a .571 OPS, upgrading at catcher needs to be a priority. There will also be more time to reason with the Colorado Rockies, who were reportedly pushing for No. 1 prospects in Goodman talks before the deadline.

Bold Prediction: Goodman goes to the Yankees for a package of SS Dax Kilby, RHP Carlos Lagrange .

Statistics courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

Buster Posey was said to be willing to listen on Devers as far back as June . If so, Devers and his $225 million remaining contract are sure to be on the block this winter.

Given how much of a nemesis Devers was to the Yankees (and to Gerrit Cole , specifically) during his time in Boston, one doubts whether the Yankees will be seriously interested. He's also not a can't-miss star at this point. Devers is still just 29, but rocking a .319 OBP and .788 OPS.

However, a powerful lefty will never not be an appealing target for the Yankees. If we end up seeing Devers in pinstripes hitting homers against the Red Sox in support of Cole, we'll have confirmation that we are living in the most chaotic timeline.
Doesn't Hurt to Ask: CF Mike Trout (LAA), CF Byron Buxton (MIN), 1B Bryce Harper (PHI), 1B Munetaka Murakami (CHW)

The Yankees will have an opening in center field once Trent Grisham files for free agency, so it especially makes sense to inquire on Trout and Buxton. Brian Cashman just shouldn't expect to get anywhere on either. Both are institutions with their respective teams, and neither has ever expressed interest in getting traded.

After what Dave Dombrowski said last year , Harper could be a different story. As a two-time MVP who can play first base and right field and who has a powerful left-handed swing, he's a perfect Yankees target on paper. Yet he also has 10-and-5 rights and can block any trade, meaning he would have to approve any move even if the Philadelphia Phillies are willing to talk.

Murakami is a wild card. He's been a hit in his debut with the Chicago White Sox, cranking 29 homers in 95 games. He's only signed through 2027, though, so you wonder if the Pale Hose could entertain offers on the slugger if potential extension talks go nowhere.

Goodman, Abrams and Neto were popular trade candidates before the trade deadline, and the Yankees were connected to at least two of them.

Because George Lombard Jr. has since taken over at shortstop, neither Abrams nor Neto is as good of a fit these days. Either could still hypothetically provide 20-20 upside at second base or third base, though, so it's best not to take them off the board altogether.

Of all the names discussed, Marte is a potential buyer-beware option for the Yankees. He is a three-time All-Star who could fit as an on-field replacement for Jazz Chisholm Jr. However, his recent absence from the Diamondbacks while receiving injury treatment would likely invite added scrutiny in New York.

As such, Goodman remains the best fit for the Yankees. A catcher who can give you 30-homer seasons is a rare thing, and he isn't even a Coors Field product. This year, he has a .900 OPS and 19 of his 34 homers on the road.
Best guess: He won't be on the Yankees next year, but he won't retire either.

As Chris Kirschner of The Athletic noted, Stanton's remaining salary is "within the range that owner Hal Steinbrenner has been willing to absorb to move on from a player." He could therefore be comfortable with simply releasing Stanton, who would then have his pick of 29 other teams with whom to chase 500 homers.
Bold Prediction: Stanton ends up with the San Diego Padres and finishes with 470 career home runs.
Who (If Anyone) Will Replace Stanton in New York?
He's not the most interesting option for the Yankees, but Goodman is the right guy for them.

Unless they want to trust in Austin Wells' recent surge to a .571 OPS, upgrading at catcher needs to be a priority. There will also be more time to reason with the Colorado Rockies, who were reportedly pushing for No. 1 prospects in Goodman talks before the deadline.
Bold Prediction: Goodman goes to the Yankees for a package of SS Dax Kilby, RHP Carlos Lagrange .
